security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and TypeScript template literals. Environment variable references are standard Upstash client configuration and do not expose secrets. One semantic issue remains: the rate-limiting example trusts x-forwarded-for without documenting proxy validation.

remediation.issue: The rate limiting example trusts the x-forwarded-for header as the client identifier.
remediation.suggestion: Use a platform-provided client IP source or validate proxy headers before using them as rate limit keys. Document the trusted proxy requirement.

semantic_findings.title: Rate Limit Identifier Uses Spoofable Header
semantic_findings.description: The rate limiting example keys requests with request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') without validating that the app is behind a trusted proxy. Direct clients can spoof this header and avoid limits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code directly trusts x-forwarded-for for the rate limit key. This is acceptable only when proxy headers are trusted, but the example omits that prerequisite.

content.user_title: Implement Redis Caching and Rate Limiting
content.value_statement: Building Redis-backed features can be error-prone. This skill provides Upstash Redis patterns for caching, invalidation, rate limiting, sessions, pub/sub, and leaderboards.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to initialize an Upstash Redis client with environment variables.
Demonstrates cache-aside reads with Redis TTL values.
Shows cache invalidation for user records and list caches.
Provides an Upstash Ratelimit sliding window example for API routes.
Includes Redis-backed session storage, pub/sub, and leaderboard examples.
limitations: Provides examples only, not a complete application or package.
Assumes existing database tables, user types, and request handlers.
Does not include tests, error handling, retries, or observability.
Does not document trusted proxy requirements for forwarded IP headers.

use_cases.title: Add API Caching
use_cases.description: Backend developers can add Redis cache-aside reads and TTL-based storage to common database queries.

use_cases.title: Protect Endpoints
use_cases.description: API teams can adapt the Upstash sliding window example to limit high-traffic routes.

use_cases.title: Prototype Redis Features
use_cases.description: Product engineers can explore sessions, pub/sub, and leaderboard patterns before building production versions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Redis Caching
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single cached read path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add Upstash Redis caching to one user lookup. Include the cache key, TTL, and invalidation point.

prompt_templates.title: Create Rate Limiting
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for protecting an API route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an Upstash Redis rate limiter for my API route. Include response headers and proxy safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Session Storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline Redis session storage for my app. Include expiration, lookup, deletion, and security considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Redis Feature Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request covering several Redis patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose Redis patterns for caching, invalidation, rate limiting, pub/sub events, and leaderboards in my service.

output_examples.input: Add Redis caching to a user lookup in a TypeScript API.
output_examples.output: A cache-aside plan using a user-specific key, a five-minute TTL, and cache population after database reads.

output_examples.input: Protect a POST endpoint from burst traffic.
output_examples.output: A sliding window rate limit design with limit, remaining, and reset response headers for rejected requests.
A session flow covering ID generation, Redis expiration, lookup by session ID, and deletion during sign-out.

best_practices: Use clear key namespaces so user, session, list, and leaderboard data do not collide.
Choose TTL values based on data freshness and user impact.
Invalidate related cache entries immediately after successful writes.
anti_patterns: Do not cache sensitive data without reviewing retention and access requirements.
Do not trust x-forwarded-for unless your deployment validates proxy headers.
Do not use one shared cache key for data that varies by user or tenant.

faq.question: Does this skill install Redis or Upstash?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript examples that assume you already have an Upstash Redis account and project configuration.

faq.question: Which provider does the skill target?
faq.answer: The examples target Upstash Redis and the Upstash Ratelimit package.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill contains portable guidance and examples for supported coding assistants.

faq.question: Does it include production hardening?
faq.answer: Only partially. You should add validation, tests, monitoring, retries, and deployment-specific security controls.

faq.question: Does it cover cache invalidation?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows deleting record-specific and list cache keys after updates.

faq.question: Does it cover Redis features beyond caching?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for rate limiting, sessions, pub/sub messages, and sorted set leaderboards.
